family_review.editorial_finding: Present phases 1, 2, and 4 in corridor context, retaining the preexisting phase 6 link and the archived master-plan link. These are distinct geographic segments of one trail, not separate archive objects.

Group corridor, trail, landscaping, and crossing records by roadway versus bicycling purpose. Keep the phased trail and 2018 refuge access project distinct; each source link appears on its single canonical page.
Preserve phases 1 and 2 as distinct construction stages alongside existing phase 3; describe dated traffic notices as historical.
Distinguish the added-lane corridor project from the adaptive-signal and fiber system; each has separate public infrastructure substance.
Place the Downtown station on Rail Runner rider information and the County valley-shelter program in ABQ RIDE historical facilities context; past route counts are presented as history.

entries.label: Bridge Boulevard Phase 2
entries.description: The County reconstruction record covers Young Avenue to La Vega Drive, with resurfacing, accessible sidewalks and ramps, bicycle lanes, adaptive signals, and street lighting. Dated traffic notices are historical; consult the County page for any new travel advisory.

entries.label: Downtown Albuquerque Rail Runner Station
entries.description: Rio Metro locates the station at the Alvarado Transportation Center, 100 1st Street SW, and gives parking, accessibility, bicycle-locker, and bus-connection information for riders.

entries.label: Eubank Trail
entries.description: The County project built a paved trail, drainage improvements, and bicycle-lane striping along Eubank Boulevard from Wilshire to Alameda; its source records 2017 construction and completion.

entries.label: Rio Bravo Boulevard Gap
entries.description: The County project added a lane in each direction between Prince Street and Second Street, alongside a multi-use trail connection, sidewalks, bicycle lanes, lighting, and signals. Its page lists July 2025 completion.

entries.label: Second Street SW Corridor Phase 2
entries.description: The County plan covers Second Street SW from Rio Bravo Boulevard to the South Diversion Channel, proposing resurfacing, sidewalks, curb and gutter drainage, lighting, and a pedestrian-bicycle bridge over the channel. The page lists construction bidding in 2029.

entries.label: Alameda Drain Trail Phase 2
entries.description: The County phase extends the shared-use trail along the Alameda Drain from Osuna Road to El Pueblo Road, with landscaping, trail amenities, and stormwater-quality features. It is part of the nine-mile master-plan corridor.

entries.label: Second Street Trail Phase 2
entries.description: The County page documents the approximately one-mile, 10-foot-wide asphalt trail along the east side of Second Street from Prosperity Avenue to Rio Bravo Boulevard, following the earlier South Diversion Channel segment.

entries.label: ABQ RIDE Valley Bus Shelters
entries.description: The County record describes its agreement with ABQ RIDE and the federally funded installation of 45 accessible, solar-powered shelters on North and South Valley routes, with route-level shelter counts. It is a historical facilities record, not a current route guide.

entries.label: Alameda Drain Trail Phase 1
entries.description: The first County phase runs beside the Alameda Drain between Montano and Osuna Roads, adding shared-use trail space, landscaping, amenities, and water-quality work at stormwater outfalls. The source reports the 2018-2019 construction period.

entries.label: Second Street Landscaping Project
entries.description: The County project used native landscaping, irrigation, and green stormwater methods along Second Street, supported by a Great Urban Parks grant and County trail bonds. The page records completion in July 2019.

entries.label: Alameda Drain Trail Phase 4
entries.description: This County trail phase runs from El Pueblo Road to Alameda Boulevard, continuing the shared-use route with landscaping and water-quality features at drain outfalls. The project page reports completion in October 2025.

entries.label: Second Street Quiet Crossing
entries.description: The County record documents road, sidewalk, curb, and gutter work needed to activate the rail quiet crossing at Second Street and Prosperity Avenue. It lists construction completion in February 2020.

entries.label: Second Street Trail Phase 1
entries.description: The first County trail phase built an approximately one-mile, 10-foot-wide asphalt route along the east side of Second Street from the South Diversion Channel to Prosperity Avenue. The page records completion in 2016.

entries.label: 118th Street Alignment Study at I-40
entries.description: The County study examines a future 118th Street SW arterial alignment from Eucariz Avenue to Ladera Drive and the location of a possible I-40 interchange, including alternatives, drainage, right-of-way, and agency coordination.

entries.label: Coors Boulevard SW Safety Project
entries.description: The County project page describes planned accessibility, lighting, and other multimodal safety improvements on Coors Boulevard between Gun Club and Blake Roads. Its design and schedule figures are dated planning information, not a current completion claim.

entries.label: Rio Grande Boulevard Bike Lane Improvements
entries.description: The County project describes widening Rio Grande Boulevard from the Los Ranchos boundary to Alameda Trail for on-street bicycle lanes, with possible sidewalk work, pavement rehabilitation, utility relocation, and irrigation-canal improvements. The page dates construction to 2017.

entries.label: Atrisco Heritage High School 118th Street Improvements
entries.description: The County added a curb and extended the trail along 118th Street at Atrisco Heritage High School. Its project page records state funding and December 2018 construction completion.

entries.label: Sage Road and Old Coors Road Intersection
entries.description: The County project added dedicated turn lanes, permanent signals, lighting, and accessible crossings at Sage Road SW and Old Coors Road SW. The page describes the intersection work as completed.

entries.label: Rio Bravo Adaptive Signals and Fiber
entries.description: The County record covers adaptive signal control and fiber between Coors and Broadway on Rio Bravo Boulevard, plus fiber on Second Street to the Animal Care facility to complete the connection. Its page labels the project in closeout.

entries.label: Central Avenue Pedestrian Hybrid Beacon
entries.description: The County installed a pedestrian hybrid beacon on Central Avenue between Texas and Utah Streets. Its project record lists design beginning in 2019 and construction completion in July 2021.

entries.label: Bridge Boulevard Phase 1
entries.description: The first County reconstruction phase addressed Bridge Boulevard west of Goff to Old Coors and Tower Road toward Coors, with intersection, sidewalk, accessibility, drainage, and lighting work. The page records construction starting in 2020.
